title: The Weather Today (Sun, Rain & Frost)

expressions.example: What's the weather like today? — It's sunny and hot.

expressions.expr: It's too windy for the sprayer.
expressions.meaning: Está ventando demais para o pulverizador.
expressions.example: We can't spray now. It's too windy for the sprayer.

expressions.expr: Does it rain a lot here?
expressions.example: Does it rain a lot here in January? — Yes, it does.
The soil is very dry. The crop needs rain.

grammar.title: Padrão: It's + clima e a diferença entre very e too
rules: Frases sobre o clima sempre começam com It's: It's hot, It's sunny, It's cold at night.
very significa 'muito' (intenso, mas normal): It's very hot today.
too significa 'demais' (passou do limite, atrapalha o trabalho): It's too wet for the tractor.
Para falar de chuva como rotina, rain é verbo com it: It rains a lot in January. / Does it rain in July?

opts: What's the weather like today?
How's the weather like today?
What the weather is today?
How much is the weather today?
quiz.why: Diga What's the weather like? ou How's the weather? — nunca misture How com like.

quiz.a: It's too windy for the sprayer.
opts: It's too windy for the sprayer.
Is too windy for the sprayer.
It's too much windy for the sprayer.
It has too windy for the sprayer.
quiz.why: Clima começa com It's, e antes de adjetivo (windy) usamos too, sem much.

quiz.a: It rains a lot in January.
opts: It rains a lot in January.
It's rain a lot in January.
It rain a lot on January.
Rains a lot in January.
quiz.why: Com it no presente simples, o verbo rain ganha -s (It rains), e meses usam in.

quiz.q: "A geada é ruim para o milho."
quiz.a: Frost is bad for the corn.
opts: Frost is bad for the corn.
Drought is bad for the corn.
Sunny is bad for the corn.
Warm is bad for the corn.
quiz.why: Frost é geada; drought é seca.

quiz.a: The field is too wet today.
opts: The field is too wet today.
The field is too dry today.
The field are too wet today.
The field is very much wet today.
quiz.why: wet = molhado/encharcado; too wet = molhado demais.
